meta.title: Simulation Lab - Where Is This Going To Break

modules.intro: Setup is in the guide, Simulation tab. Run it on your own part.
modules.title: Your Study
modules.aiNote: Unrestricted for driving SolidWorks. Ask it anything, as often as you want.

blocks.content:
Upload one screenshot of your solved plot with the color scale showing.

Mark two things on it:

1. Where it goes red.
2. Where your part is thinnest.

Write the red spot in your notebook before you leave. Tomorrow starts from it.

items: Ran on my own V1 part
Both faces split, fixture and load on the outer halves

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Own part, both faces split with fixture and load on the outer halves, Nylon 101, force on Selected direction.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Study runs but one setup condition is wrong or missing.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No study, or run on a file that is not the student's own part.

rubric.criterion: Study set up as the guide specifies, on the student's own part

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Color scale visible, both marks present and distinguishable.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Plot uploaded with only one of the two marked, or the scale cropped out.

rubric.criterion: Screenshot shows a solved plot with the red spot and the thinnest section marked

modules.intro: Two questions. Two sentences each is plenty.
modules.title: What You See
modules.aiNote: Ask it what a von Mises plot is. Do not ask it where your red spot is. You will be asked to point at it.

blocks.prompt: Where is the red, described on your part and not on your screen? Same place as your thinnest section, or somewhere else?
Your study also shows a load number. Why is that number wrong for your hook when the red spot is right?

blocks.content:
### Sources

- Hook Design and Manufacturing Guide, Simulation tab and Where Hooks Break.
- SOLIDWORKS Help, help.solidworks.com.
- Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design, 10th edition, Budynas and Nisbett, McGraw-Hill, 2015.
- IDEA AI Use Policy.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Names a feature of the hook rather than a region of the screen, and says whether it coincides with the thinnest section.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Red spot named on the part, comparison missing or unclear.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Describes where the red sits in the picture rather than on the part.

rubric.criterion: Locates the red spot on the part and compares it to the thinnest section

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Ties the wrong number to the substituted material or the printed structure, and says the stress pattern follows the geometry, which is real.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Says the number is unreliable with a real reason, but does not say why the location still holds.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Nothing written, or restates the rule with no reason.

rubric.criterion: Explains why magnitude does not transfer from this study but location does
